messages:
anya: Heads-up — we got a customer hitting 413s on POST /v1/embeddings. Payload is a mix of 1536- and 3072-dim vectors in the same array. Repro attached below.

ben: Can you paste the exact body they sent? 413 could be total bytes or server-side reject on mixed dims.

anya: sample payload (sanitized):
```json
{
  \"inputs\": [
    {\"id\":\"a\", \"vector\": [0.1, 0.2, ...1536 items...]},
    {\"id\":\"b\", \"vector\": [0.3, 0.4, ...3072 items...]}
  ]
}
```

maria: ugh mixed dims. Our current router assumes uniform dim per request for batching/kv cache. If we accept mixed dims we either: 
- split into per-dim batches server-side (adds latency and complexity), or
- reject with a clear 4xx that tells the user to split.
Which do we want as the default?

kevin: telemetry + quota implications here. If we silently split, token/embedding unit accounting could double-count or misattribute to routes/models. Need a consistent metric.

sam: +1 on explicit error with helpful message. We can provide a client-side helper in SDK to auto-split (opt-in). Avoid surprises server-side.

anya: The customer expects simple client behavior. They like a single call. If we force-split, the UX is better but we need to update console and docs + add metrics.

ben: Proposal: server returns 413 when total bytes > 10MB, and 422 with a new code when payload contains mixed dims: {\"error\":\"mixed_embedding_dims\", \"detail\":\"split per-dim or use ?auto_split=true\"}.

maria: What about adding ?auto_split=true query param that triggers splitting logic and emits a telemetry event: embed.split.count and embed.split.extra_latency_ms? Then default is reject.

kevin: If we add auto_split, we must tag the downstream model calls with the original request id so billing/quotas map back. Otherwise quotas will be inconsistent. Also need a telemetry dimension for route/variant so we can A/B.

sam: Console UX: show a banner in the route config when a route supports auto_split and list the cost delta (approx). Also allow toggling at route-level or account-level.

anya: Implementation note: splitter should be cheap. Pseudocode:
```python
# group inputs by len(vector)
by_dim = defaultdict(list)
for item in inputs:
  by_dim[len(item['vector'])].append(item)
# for each dim -> call embeddings model for that dim
```
But we need to cap concurrency to avoid bursting GPUs.

ben: Good. Also add rejection message for huge single-vector sizes (e.g., > 50k dims) — that should stay 413.

kevin: Telemetry list to add: 
- embed.request_size_bytes
- embed.input_count
- embed.dim_cardinality (how many unique dims per request)
- embed.split_count
- embed.splits_latency_ms
Also tag with route, model_version, and request_id.

maria: For rollout plan: add ?auto_split on a special canary route (route config flag). Start 1% of traffic for 48h, monitor embed.split_count and error rates. Ramp if stable.

sam: Also add console telemetry panel showing "mixed-dims" rate and split overhead. Product will want cost estimates in USD per 10k splits.

infra-bot: deploybot: New candidate: embed-splitter-v1 queued for canary.

anya: Action items: @maria implement splitter (server) + telemetry hooks. @ben update API errors and SDK helper. @kevin wire billing tags. @sam add console banner + metrics card. I'll own rollout plan.

ben: Quick question — should SDK auto-split by default with a big warn? That would be easiest for users but hides costs.

kevin: Don't default to auto-split in SDK. Make it opt-in and surface cost. We need explicit consent.

maria: I'll spin up a PR that implements splitting and emits embed.split_count and embed.dim_cardinality. Will include a feature flag: EMBED_AUTO_SPLIT.

anya: Thanks. I'll post a follow-up with the exact error payload shape and the canary schedule. :thumbsup:

sam: 👍 please include console mockup for banner text: \"This route will automatically split mixed-dimension embed requests (may increase cost)\"

ben: Leaving a note: tests to add — split correctness, header passthrough, request_id propagation, billing attribution.

kevin: Also add e2e to ensure quotas/usage graphs show combined usage correctly.

anya: Last note — we should update our public docs and quickstart SDK snippet. If anyone wants to disagree with reject-by-default, speak now or on the PR.

maria: will do PR today.

ben: Thanks all.

infra-bot: deploybot: Canary started for embed-splitter-v1 at 1782500200 (1% traffic). Monitor: embed.split_count, 5xx rate.

anya: Filed follow-up ticket: EMBEDS-412 in backlog for docs + SDK helper.
